That si_dimension supports the candidate exponents M=1, L=-1, T=-1 (others zero). The record therefore directly validates the viscous-dimension assignment for mu_w in the original problem.

The ledger variable 'rho' denotes local fluid mass density. The ledger variable 'mu' is the local dynamic viscosity. That si_dimension supports the candidate exponents M=1, L=-1, T=-1 (others zero), so the record directly validates the ledger vector for 'mu'.

The ledger variable 'u_tau' is the friction velocity. The KB record pq_friction_velocity defines friction velocity (symbols u_tau, uτ), provides the same definition used in wall-bounded turbulence (u_tau = sqrt(tau_w/rho)), and lists si_dimension 'L T^-1' (velocity). That directly supports the ledger assignment of exponents L=1 and T=-1 (others zero). The record therefore applies to the ledger variable and justifies its SI exponent vector.
